t.1.35.1: Having heard the words of Elāpatra, O best of the twice-born, all the Nāgas, their hearts delighted, applauded him, crying, "Well said, well said!"
t.1.35.2: From that time on, Vāsuki guarded that maiden, his sister Jaratkāru, and he attained the highest joy.
t.1.35.3: Then, when no very great length of time had seemingly passed, all the Devas and Asuras churned the abode of Varuṇa, the ocean.
t.1.35.4: There the serpent Vāsuki, best of the mighty, became the churning rope; and having completed that task, they went to the Grandfather.
t.1.35.5: Then the gods, together with Vāsuki, said to the Grandfather: "O Blessed One, this Vāsuki, frightened by the curse, is sorely tormented."
t.1.35.6: O god, you ought to draw out this thorn lodged in his mind, born of his mother's curse, for he desires the welfare of his kinsmen.
t.1.35.7: For this king of the Nāgas has always been our well-wisher and has done what pleases us. Show him your grace, lord of the gods, and calm the fever of his mind.
t.1.35.8: O immortals, it was by me alone, through my mind, that this word was granted, the word that the serpent Elāpatra formerly spoke to him.
t.1.35.10: That Jaratkāru has been born, a twice-born devoted to fierce austerity. To him let this one, at the proper time, give his sister Jaratkāru.
t.1.35.9: Let this lord of the Nāgas carry out that timely counsel accordingly. Those who are wicked will perish, but not those who practise dharma.
t.1.35.11: The words that were then spoken by the serpent Elāpatra for the good of the snakes, O gods, are just so, and not otherwise.
t.1.35.13: When the lord Jaratkāru should wish to choose a wife, come quickly and tell me; that will be for our good.
t.1.35.12: Having then heard this word of the Grandfather, that lord of the Nāgas appointed many serpents, ever diligent, to keep watch over Jaratkāru.
